## LLM Recipe

### 1.8 Distillation &amp; Model Compression

#### [Strong Starts, Simple Recipes: Unified Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation from Multimodal Specialists](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34397>)

This comparative study tests how merging same-base multimodal specialists before on-policy distillation changes the value of initialization, sampling and training objectives. For one Qwen3-VL model family, a uniform merge followed by short full-vocabulary distillation provides a strong integration baseline without coefficient search or elaborate domain schedules.

#### [Distilling Kimi-K3.1-Pro into Qwen3.8-27B: Teaching a model a new language](<https://www.together.ai/blog/distilling-kimi-into-qwen>)

TogetherAI tests sequence-level teacher distillation with a small replay mixture to teach Lao translation while preserving the student’s Thai. Its Qwen3.8-27B LoRA study raises Lao chrF++ from 5.5 to 44.3 while Thai rises from 46.7 to 47.8, illustrating why adaptation should measure nearby skills and mix in data that protects them.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.4 Retrieval &amp; Knowledge Integration

#### [ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34366>)

ConTra trains small models to write a reusable context prefix for each document chunk, combining frozen embedding/reranking feedback with source-support and length penalties so both retrieval stages can read the missing context. With top-15 Qwen reranking, its 2B generator reports macro nDCG@10 of 0.8525 on eight ConTEB tasks and 0.6692 across five RealContextBench collections plus three context conditions, improving on same-size prompted prefixes. Its 7.74× speedup over a prompted 9B generator measures offline indexing of one short-document subset on an H100, offering a scoped quality–indexing-cost tradeoff rather than a general query-latency claim.

### 2.8 Agent Evaluation &amp; Security

#### [The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33605>)

ARGUS tests how tool-service failures can make agents complete workflows while silently dropping security requirements, then separates persistent obligations from changeable recovery plans and enforces them at sensitive effects. In its local MCP/Skill evaluation, guarded configurations have no observed protection loss across 576 scheduled runs, while recovery guidance improves protected completion for some models; this offers a concrete design for recovery gates under complete mediation rather than a production security guarantee.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.6 Low-Precision &amp; Efficient Execution

#### [MixMoMo: Mixed-Precision GPU–NPU Execution of Large MoE Models on Mobile Devices](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33981>)

MixMoMo chooses expert precision from offline calibration and current activations, then splits same-precision work between a phone’s GPU and neural processing unit. Batched dequantization and profiled scheduling connect precision choices to actual hardware costs, helping large mixture-of-experts models execute on mobile devices. Across three models on two OnePlus phones, the authors report an average 1.53× decoding speedup over the strongest tested mixed-precision baseline, while detailed quality evidence covers only one model.
